clue.text: Display out of place

parts.note: EX is a prefix meaning out of or former
a position is a place

explanation.surface: Something has been put on show in the wrong spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibition or public show of goods is a display.

clue.text: Where emperor was confined in hotel basement

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words hotel basement, running across the gap

explanation.surface: An emperor has been locked away in the cellar of a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was exiled to this Mediterranean island in 1814, an example of where an emperor was confined.

clue.text: Nipper stuck here — has one no proper ink?

definitions.text: Nipper stuck here — has one no proper ink?

parts.words: Nipper stuck here — has one no proper ink?
parts.note: a nipper is a small child kept penned in while playing; the second half jokes that this kind of pen is not a writing pen and holds no ink

explanation.surface: A child is trapped somewhere, and someone asks whether a pen has run dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A small enclosure where a toddler is put to play safely is exactly where a nipper is stuck.

clue.text: As anticipated, another visitor is announced

indicators.note: announced signals that the words are spoken, giving a sound rather than a spelling

parts.note: a second guest is another visitor, and 'second guest's' run together sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: A butler announces the arrival of a further visitor, just as expected.
explanation.definitionFit: To second-guess is to anticipate or predict someone's action, so the past form means foreseen.

clue.text: Thought male should be clothed in blue

indicators.note: a male wrapped in blue means one word goes inside the other

parts.note: blue is the colour of the UK Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a man ought to be dressed in blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an idea or a line of thought put forward to explain something.

clue.text: Oversight of old church

parts.note: a mission is a church or chapel serving a district

explanation.surface: Some failing on the part of an old church is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is something left out by mistake, a thing missed.

clue.text: Gnome's shortened coat

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a gnome is a pithy saying or maxim; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A garden gnome is wearing a cropped coat.
explanation.walkthrough: A gnome here is not a garden figure but an aphorism, a maxim; drop its last letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a long coat reaching the ankles.

clue.text: Question doubting my talent? Charming

definitions.meaning: a speaker unsure of their ability asks whether they are capable

explanation.definitionFit: A charming person is friendly and pleasant, which is what amiable describes.

clue.text: Certainly not late home, wanting fun

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
fun is a good time

explanation.surface: Someone heads home early, not wanting any fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving with time to spare means being early enough, so certainly not late.

clue.text: Name of woman bishop introduced to church in a way

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, which comes first here

indicators.note: church is placed inside a way

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: A female bishop is presented to her church.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanche is a woman's given name, as in Blanche DuBois.

clue.text: Having little time to dip into Chinese book is irritating

indicators.note: the time briefly goes into the book, one piece inside the other

parts.note: the I Ching is an ancient Chinese book of divination
T is a short abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone with no time to browse a Chinese classic finds that annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Itching, as a skin feeling, is irritating, causing a wish to scratch.

clue.text: Steady worker put out by disturbances in buildings

indicators.note: the worker is put out, removed from the word for steady

parts.note: steady means constant
an ant is the crossword's usual worker
ructions are rows or disturbances

explanation.surface: A reliable labourer is thrown off the job by trouble on the building sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steady worker' looks like one person, but steady is CONSTANT and the worker ANT is removed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Constructions are things built, such as buildings.

clue.text: Nipper soon thrown in jail

indicators.note: thrown suggests letters being tossed into disorder

explanation.surface: A young thief will soon be locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: An open prison is a jail with minimal security for low-risk inmates.

clue.text: Word used for male relative the world over

indicators.note: over in a down-reading sense means turned back to front

parts.note: an orb is a sphere, the world

explanation.surface: A term for a brother is in use across the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Bro is a colloquial shortening of brother.

clue.text: Player who has no prior arrangements?

definitions.text: Player who has no prior arrangements?

parts.words: Player who has no prior arrangements?
parts.note: a performer who makes things up on the spot rather than working from rehearsed material

explanation.definitionFit: A performer who extemporises plays without anything prepared in advance.

clue.text: Take control of area in grip of disease

indicators.note: the area is held inside the disease

parts.note: mange is a skin disease of animals

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of a region gripped by an epidemic.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage is to run or be in charge of something.

clue.text: Supporter observed Nottingham players surrounding ball at back of net

indicators.note: the club's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Nottingham Forest is an English football club
O is shaped like a ball

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so at back of net asks for the final letter of that word

explanation.surface: A fan watches the Nottingham team after the ball hits the back of the net.
explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club. 'observed' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A footrest supports the feet, so it is a supporter.

clue.text: Tricks for assimilating a new European language

indicators.note: the tricks take in the other letters

parts.note: japes are jokes or tricks

explanation.surface: Playful methods help someone pick up a new European tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese is the language spoken in Japan.

clue.text: Soldier beginning to recite poem to sweetheart

indicators.note: the first letter of recite

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem
leman is an old word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A soldier starts reading a poem to his beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifleman is an infantry soldier armed with a rifle.

clue.text: Bird in a flat spin

indicators.note: a spin throws the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird is flapping about in somebody's apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantail is a pigeon or flycatcher with a fan-shaped tail.

clue.text: Fool getting shot?

explanation.definitionFit: Dumdum means both a silly person and a soft-nosed expanding bullet.

clue.text: Food and drink served briefly round new eating area

indicators.note: the food and drink go around the new letter

parts.note: diet is the food one eats

indicators.note: briefly means the drink loses its last letter

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Refreshments are served quickly in a new dining spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinette is a small area or alcove set aside for eating meals.

clue.text: Reportedly tense spots

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word sounds like another when said

parts.note: to flex a muscle is to tense it

explanation.surface: Rumour has it some places are anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Flecks are small marks or specks, which is what spots can be.

clue.text: Seamen mostly brought back in trailer

indicators.note: brought back means the letters are read in reverse
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the navy is a body of seamen

explanation.surface: Sailors are being returned home in a trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A van can be a covered trailer or wagon pulled behind a vehicle, as a horse van is.

clue.text: One-time composer repulsed an infectious illness

indicators.note: the composer's name is given with just one T for time, so one T goes

parts.note: Scarlatti was an Italian baroque composer

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A former composer is said to have fought off a contagious disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' reads as 'former', but it asks for SCARLATTI with only one T (time).
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlatina is scarlet fever, an infectious bacterial illness.

clue.text: Stupid measure introduced by US attorney

parts.note: DA is district attorney in the US
FT, foot, is a measure

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor brings in a foolish new law.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is an informal word for silly or stupid.

clue.text: Curiously, senate admits Democrat who doesn't have a seat?

indicators.note: admits means the jumbled word takes in the letter
curiously signals that the letters are odd, out of order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: Oddly, the senate lets in a Democrat without a place to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A standee is a person who has to stand, having no seat, at a show or on transport.

clue.text: Concealing article in rubbish, spies for country

indicators.note: the spies hide the rest inside them

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

indicators.note: the article goes inside the rubbish

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Secret agents hide an item in the trash for a foreign power.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Burn food cooked on gridiron? That's no good

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is removed

parts.note: a grill is a dish of food cooked on a gridiron

explanation.surface: Food cooked on a griddle gets burnt and is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: Burn is not scorching: in Scotland a burn is a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A burn in Scots is a small stream, and a rill is a little brook.

clue.text: Ongoing parking trouble in streets

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: There are continuing problems with parking in the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent means continuing over a long time, so it means ongoing.
